summary: numbox/core/variable/variable.py is a clean, well-factored pure-Python graph module (dataclasses + ABC; no structref/refcount surface despite the target notes — those live in compile_kernel.py). Two minor, low-severity design nits only: a piece of dead defensive code and an O(N)-per-key linear scan where a Variable-keyed lookup already exists. No duplication or over-complexity worth reworking.

findings.title: Dead defensive branch in _topological_order (string normalization already done by sole caller)
findings.claim: _topological_order re-runs `if isinstance(required, str): required = [required]`, but its only caller, Graph.compile, already normalizes `required` to a list at lines 441-442 before passing it in. The branch can never execute, contradicting both the `required: list[str]` annotation and the comment that this is an internal helper. Harmless, but it is dead code that suggests the helper has a second, untrusted entry point that does not exist.
findings.evidence:
Caller compile (lines 441-447): `if isinstance(required, str):
    required = [required]
...
ordered_variables, used_external_vars = self._topological_order(required)`. Helper signature (line 473): `def _topological_order(self, required: list[str])`. Helper body (lines 478-479): `if isinstance(required, str):
    required = [required]`. grep confirms compile is the only caller of _topological_order in numbox and test.
findings.recommendation: Drop the duplicate isinstance/normalization at lines 478-479; the contract is already `list[str]`. Surgical, zero behavior change.

findings.title: recompute resolves intra-graph changed variables by O(N) linear scan over ordered_nodes
findings.claim: For each changed variable that is not an external, recompute does `next(n.variable for n in self.ordered_nodes if n.variable.qual_name() == qual_name)`, an O(N) scan (and a qual_name() string build per node) for every such changed name, i.e. O(N*k) per recompute call. CompiledGraph already holds Variable-keyed structures (self.dependents is keyed by Variable, ordered_nodes is enumerable once), so a name->Variable index built alongside dependents in __post_init__ would make this O(1) per key. Purely a maintainability/efficiency nit; results are correct.
findings.recommendation: In __post_init__, build a `self._by_qual_name: dict[str, Variable]` (or dict[str, CompiledNode]) alongside dependents and look up directly in recompute. Local, low risk; aligns with the affected_cache/dependents precomputation already in this class.
